candidate.title: PV Care OS: white-label multi-vendor fleet triage for Polish installers
candidate.thesis: Evidence: Poland had 1,636,673 renewable micro-installations at the end of 2025, 99.9% of them photovoltaic, while the national energy ombudsman reports recurring prosumer problems involving voltage-triggered shutdowns, confusing net-billing, meters, and misconfigured inverters. IEA PVPS separately identifies disconnected PV digital tools, trapped lifecycle information, and inadequate interoperability, while EU evidence points to shortages in green installation and maintenance skills. Inference: a white-label operating system for regional installers could unify inverter, meter, bill, warranty, and service-history data; remotely triage anomalies; prepare customer, warranty, and DSO evidence packs; and dispatch scarce technicians only when physical work is justified. The initial wedge is a paid pilot through the founder's family renewable-energy company, expanding into recurring per-site software fees and transaction fees on repairs, storage retrofits, and repowering.

fingerprint.customer: Polish regional PV installers, O&M providers, and electrical-service firms responsible for portfolios of residential and small-commercial PV systems.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An inverter alert, unexplained bill increase, production drop, voltage shutdown, warranty issue, or customer complaint forces staff to inspect several disconnected portals and records before deciding whether remote action, a DSO case, or a technician visit is required.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer or O&M provider pays a recurring portfolio subscription per monitored site; additional revenue is earned when a diagnosed case becomes an out-of-warranty repair, inspection, battery or EMS retrofit, or repowering job.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: White-label B2B SaaS plus managed service: multi-vendor monitoring ingestion, anomaly prioritisation, AI-assisted diagnosis, automated evidence and customer communication, warranty workflow, technician dispatch, and upgrade recommendations.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Begin with a measured portfolio pilot inside the founder's parents' renewable-installation company, then sell through inverter and storage distributors, regional installer partnerships, and portfolio audits demonstrating recovered production or avoided truck rolls.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned cross-vendor dataset linking telemetry, configuration, symptoms, field findings, remedies, costs, and outcomes improves diagnosis and dispatch rules; accumulated site histories and embedded service workflows increase switching costs.

founder_fit: Uses the founder's data-science and AI-automation strengths for anomaly detection, evidence reconciliation, and workflow automation.
The parents' seven-person renewable-energy company offers unusually direct access to a real pilot portfolio, technicians, workflow observations, and early customer conversations.
A software-first pilot can be operated alongside employment within the founder's five-hour daily limit and without a public-facing personal brand.
The proposed validation budget fits within approximately 100,000 PLN and can be gated on paid design partners before substantial spending.
The Polish starting market provides local-language, regulatory, billing, and DSO workflow specificity before any wider EU expansion.

economics.pricing: Inference to test: 8–15 PLN per monitored site per month with a 1,000–2,000 PLN monthly portfolio minimum, plus an 8–12% orchestration fee on paid repairs and upgrades.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Inference: monitoring and automated triage could support roughly 75–90% software gross margin; technician coordination and managed cases would be materially lower-margin, so profitability depends on keeping most cases remote or partner-fulfilled.
economics.acquisition_route: Proposed: convert one family-company portfolio into a quantified case study, then acquire installers through distributor introductions and fixed-price portfolio audits rather than broad consumer marketing.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Inference: monitoring recurs for the life of each enrolled site, while faults, inspections, warranty events, storage retrofits, and repowering create repeat paid events; retention is unproven and could be weak if free OEM portals are sufficient.
economics.capital_required_pln: Inference: 40,000–100,000 PLN for the first integrations, secure data handling, insurance and legal review, and a paid pilot; further integrations should be funded from customer demand.
economics.founder_time: Proposed initial load: 15–25 founder hours per week, with family-company technicians handling authorised field validation and physical work.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Inference scenario, not a forecast: reaching 60,000 monitored sites at 10 PLN per month produces 7.2 million PLN annual subscription revenue before transaction fees. At approximately 25% EBITDA, a 4x EBITDA valuation and 70% founder ownership imply about 5.0 million PLN of founder equity value. This would require roughly 3.7% of Poland's 2025 prosumer base, repeatable installer-channel sales, and likely five to seven years; retained earnings are not added again as personal wealth.

claims.statement: Evidence: at the end of 2025 Poland had 1,636,673 renewable micro-installations with almost 13.9 GW of capacity; 99.9% were PV and 1,612,450 belonged to prosumers.

Evidence: Poland's energy ombudsman reported that nearly one-third of 2025 electricity applications came from prosumers and described voltage-triggered PV shutdowns, disputed net-billing and meter readings, and cases involving incorrectly configured inverters or heat pumps.

Evidence: IEA PVPS reports that PV digitalisation efforts remain disconnected, lifecycle information becomes trapped, and interoperability and standardisation are needed; it also identifies predictive maintenance and integrated monitoring as ways to reduce downtime and operating costs.

Evidence: a July 2026 Cedefop brief says demand is growing for people who install and maintain renewable-energy systems and reports that 79% of EU firms view skills shortages as a barrier to investment.

Inference: combining a large distributed installed base, documented prosumer troubleshooting problems, fragmented PV data, and scarce technical labour creates a plausible willingness-to-pay hypothesis for remote triage and service orchestration, but none of the cited sources validates the proposed product, buyer, or price.

contrary_evidence: Evidence limitation: ombudsman applications are self-selected disputes and do not establish the incidence or monetary cost of problems across Poland's full prosumer base.
Evidence limitation: the IEA PVPS report covers the broader PV lifecycle and is not proof that small Polish installers will pay for a shared operating layer.
Market counterpoint: inverter manufacturers already provide monitoring portals, so a paid aggregator must demonstrate materially better diagnosis, workflow automation, or avoided site visits.
Operational counterpoint: software cannot repair grid-voltage constraints or electrical faults; many cases will still require a licensed local technician or action by the DSO.
uncertainties: Number of sites each target installer still actively supports and the share accessible through usable APIs, exports, or customer-authorised credentials.
Baseline labour cost, truck-roll rate, resolution time, lost generation, and support burden against which ROI can be measured.
Installers' willingness to pay recurring per-site fees versus passing a consumer care-plan charge through to system owners.
Whether vendor terms permit the required data access and whether a sufficiently broad multi-vendor integration set is economical.
Actual conversion and margin on repairs, battery or EMS retrofits, and repowering recommendations.
Sales-cycle length and whether distributor partnerships can deliver portfolios without high-touch founder-led selling.
risks: Cybersecurity, GDPR, credential custody, and remote-control exposure across household energy systems.
Incorrect diagnosis or automated advice could create electrical-safety, warranty, financial, or professional-liability claims.
Vendor API restrictions or portal changes could make integrations unreliable and expensive to maintain.
Installers under margin pressure may resist another subscription despite operational savings.
A family-company pilot could overfit the product to one firm's brands, geography, and practices.
OEMs, distributors, energy retailers, or established monitoring platforms could bundle equivalent workflow features.

evidence_sources.title: URE report: The number of RES micro-installations in Poland has already exceeded 1.6 million
evidence_sources.one-sentence relevance: Establishes the scale, PV dominance, prosumer concentration, and dual settlement regimes of Poland's distributed micro-installation base.

evidence_sources.title: Sprawozdanie za 2025 r.
evidence_sources.publisher: Coordinator for Negotiations at the President of the Energy Regulatory Office
evidence_sources.one-sentence relevance: Documents recurring Polish prosumer problems involving shutdowns, billing, meters, configuration, and multi-party resolution workflows.

evidence_sources.title: Digitalisation and Digital Twins in Photovoltaic Systems
evidence_sources.publisher: IEA Photovoltaic Power Systems Programme, Task 13
evidence_sources.one-sentence relevance: Identifies fragmented PV digital tools, trapped information, interoperability needs, and the operating benefits of integrated analytics and predictive maintenance.

evidence_sources.title: New study maps the jobs driving Europe's green transition
evidence_sources.one-sentence relevance: Supports the specialist-scarcity premise by documenting growing renewable installation and maintenance demand and widespread skills constraints.
